text:
elaine_support: Heads-up — BrightWave (prod) reporting repeated tool/function-call failures starting ~08:12 UTC. They see 400/422s coming out of our function-caller with 'schema validation' errors. Customer impact: their search flows fall back to model-only and some KPI regressions. :rotating_light:

elaine_support: quick log snippet from their error dump:
```
2026-03-12T08:12:34.512Z ERROR function_runner: SchemaValidationError: extra fields in args: 'regionCode'
request_id=req_0a1b2c3d
route=call-search-tool-v2 model=gptx-infer-1
payload={"tool":"search_tool_v2","args":{"query":"kubernetes error","regionCode":"us-west-2"}}
stack: FunctionCaller.validate_args -> jsonschema.validate -> raises
```

martin_eng: do we have the original request body from the customer or the routed normalized payload? need both. also which router policy picked search_tool_v2 vs search_tool?

elaine_support: pasted request from their client (redacted customer headers):
```http
POST /v1/responses HTTP/1.1
Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "input":"find logs for pod crash",
  "tool_call":{"name":"search_tool_v2","arguments":"{\"query\":\"kubernetes error\",\"regionCode\":\"us-west-2\"}"}
}
```
Note: their SDK accidentally stringified arguments (arguments is a string containing JSON) — we see a double-encoded args blob.

anya_sre: ah — double-encoded args can make our JSON schema validator see a string where it expects an object, but that usually errors as type mismatch not extra field. The log shows 'extra fields' which suggests we ran coercion/unpack step but didn't remove unknown keys. Did we recently flip strict_schema_enforcement on the router?

deploy_bot: config_change: feature/strict_schema_enforcement toggled ON in prod at 2026-03-12T07:59:03Z by mart_restricts (deploy id: d-20260312-978).

martin_eng: that matches. Strict mode will reject unknown keys rather than drop them. Two issues: (1) SDK double-encoding -> server receives arguments as string. (2) our unpack/coercion path attempted to parse the string, produced an object containing both expected fields and an unexpected top-level 'regionCode' (BrightWave relies on our router to drop extra vendor fields historically). Now strict mode fails.

sam_reliability: proposal: 1) hotfix to make the function-caller tolerant for a short window: if arguments is string, attempt JSON.parse and then run a permissive schema pass that ignores unknown keys (log them). 2) rollback strict_schema_enforcement toggle until we patch upstream. We should do 1 immediately to reduce customer impact.

elaine_support: customer wants a mitigation now — they can patch SDK but won't be quick. Can we enable a per-tenant compatibility shim?

martin_eng: actionable steps I can run: a) push a 1-line runtime guard that tries to parse string args and catches JSON.parse errors, b) when strict_schema flag is on, fallback to permissive validation for any request with request_id pattern req_* for the next 60m. I'll prepare a minimal patch and request emergency approval.

anya_sre: ops_oncall — can you open an incident, set severity=high, notify CS to offer credit and temporary workaround? Also include the deployment change in the incident timeline.

ops_oncall: incident created: INC-2026-0312-12 (severity=high). Pager duty rung. Notifying BrightWave CSM. Adding remediation notes and owner tags. :white_check_mark:

martin_eng: hotfix diff I tested locally:
```diff
- args_obj = body['tool_call']['arguments']
- validate(args_obj)
+ raw_args = body['tool_call']['arguments']
+ args_obj = raw_args
+ if isinstance(raw_args, str):
+     try:
+         args_obj = json.loads(raw_args)
+     except Exception:
+         # leave as-is, validator will catch it
+         args_obj = raw_args
+ # permissive check when strict mode is enabled and tenant flagged for compat
+ if strict_schema and tenant_has_compat_shim(tenant_id):
+     validate_permissive(args_obj)
+ else:
+     validate_strict(args_obj)
```
I can push to prod behind a feature flag for BrightWave only.

sam_reliability: ok push that behind a rollout flag. Also add a metric that counts how often we auto-coerce string->object and how many unknown keys we drop. We need observability.

elaine_support: I've told BrightWave CSM we'll do a targeted fix within the hour and follow up with a root-cause and credit. They've provided 3 failing request_ids: req_0a1b2c3d, req_0a1b2c70, req_0a1b2c91 — attaching to INC.

martin_eng: starting the patch now. Will post deploy id and verification steps. Verification: re-run their curl with stringified arguments and ensure router no longer returns 4xx and tool is invoked.

sam_reliability: follow-up: after hotfix we should schedule a small postmortem to decide whether strict_schema is safe as a global default or needs gradual rollout + tenant opt-in. Also consider updating SDK to error earlier when stringifying args.

elaine_support: thanks team — I'll keep BrightWave updated. Please post the deploy id and ETA in this thread. :eyes:
